doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

chapter: Road life, race and Woody Herman/Tommy Dorsey
title: Meeting his wife in Ina Ray Hutton's band and marrying
summary: Tired of the road, Igoe meets his future wife in Hutton's chorus line in Covington and marries while with Woody Herman.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You eventually got — did you get tired of the road?

Oh I got tired of the road, yeah. I was with Ina Ray Hutton’s band and we had played a big nightclub in New York called the Latin Quarter when there was a Latin Quarter. It was like the Copacabana, with showgirls and all this kind of stuff — with Ina Ray Hutton’s band. Then we went out to Covington, Kentucky. Now Covington, Kentucky is just across the river from Cincinnati. And they had a miniature Las Vegas there, three casinos I think. Not like a casino today, but you could gamble, roulette wheel and blackjack and all that stuff. So we were at a place called the Lookout House with Ina Ray Hutton’s band. And they had a big show built around Ina Ray Hutton that they had made from the — modeled on the Latin Quarter thing, like a package. Then they had eight dancing girls. I had to go to Covington, Kentucky to meet a girl from Brooklyn. That’s how my wife and I met.
Yeah. She was in the chorus line.

Yeah. And she says, “you used to try to louse us up every night with that two bar solo you played, we’d all get out of step.” So I think you mentioned being on the road. So I got married, it must have been a year or two after that. We got married. And I was with Woody’s band. And he gave me two weeks off to get married. So we came home and we got — nothing special, no big wedding or anything like that.
You weren’t throwing sandwiches, were you?
No, no, nothing like that. I think we went to the local tavern. So anyway — oh I remember our wedding night my wife and I saw two Charles Dickens movies.
